The approach already has clinical support. SPY002 produced 33% clinical remission and 42% endoscopic improvement at week 12 in ulcerative colitis. (NYSE:ABBV) spent years preparing investors for the decline of Humira, once one of the best-selling medicines in the world. Its fiscal Q2 2026 results provide some of the clearest evidence yet that the company's replacement strategy might be working. Its worldwide revenue increased 10.2% to $16.99 billion, supported by strong growth in immunology and neuroscience. However, AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) progress is becoming increasingly dependent on a limited number of major products. While Skyrizi and Rinvoq are more than compensating for Humira's decline, weaker results in oncology and aesthetics demonstrate that growth is not equally distributed across the portfolio. The strongest part of AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) investment case is the continued expansion of Skyrizi and Rinvoq. Skyrizi revenue increased 24.4% to $5.51 billion, while Rinvoq revenue rose 24.5% to $2.53 billion. Together, the two medicines generated more than $8 billion during the quarter, compared with $756 million from Humira. These results suggest that AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV) has successfully transferred much of its immunology leadership to newer products rather than simply attempting to protect Humira's declining franchise. Total immunology revenue grew 15.1% to $8.79 billion despite Humira sales falling 35.9%. AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV) is also finding growth outside immunology. Neuroscience revenue increased 20.3% to $3.23 billion, supported by several products rather than a single medicine. Vraylar sales rose 18.9% to $1.07 billion, Botox Therapeutic increased 12.2% to $1.04 billion, and Qulipta grew 30.9% to $350 million. Vyalev, AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) treatment for advanced Parkinson's disease, contributed $256 million. Profitability remained strong as well. Adjusted diluted EPS increased 22.9% to $3.65, despite including a $0.17-per-share unfavorable impact from acquired research and development and milestone expenses. AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV) also reported an adjusted operating margin of 48.3%, indicating that revenue growth continued to translate into substantial earnings. AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) increasing dependence on Skyrizi and Rinvoq creates concentration risk, as the two products accounted for approximately 47% of total quarterly revenue. Their current momentum is strong, but any future regulatory, competitive, or pricing pressure affecting either franchise could have a disproportionate effect on companywide growth. Other parts of AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) portfolio were less impressive. Oncology revenue declined 1.5% to $1.65 billion, primarily reflecting a 29.4% decline in Imbruvica sales. Although Venclexta grew 11.6% and Elahere increased 33.1%, they were not sufficient to return the entire oncology portfolio to growth. Aesthetics also remained subdued, as portfolio revenue increased only 0.3% on a reported basis and declined 0.9% operationally. Continued weakness in aesthetics could limit AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) ability to develop a more balanced growth profile. The company also lowered its adjusted EPS guidance from $13.91–$14.11 to $13.87–$14.07. Although this reduction reflects the anticipated dilution from the proposed Apogee Therapeutics acquisition rather than deterioration in AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) existing operations, the deal introduces additional execution and financial risk. AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) quarter strengthens the argument that its post-Humira transition is succeeding. Skyrizi and Rinvoq continue to deliver substantial growth, while neuroscience is emerging as a meaningful second engine. The principal concern for the company can be seen as going beyond AbbVie's (NYSE:ABBV) replacement of Humira to broadening its growth beyond two dominant immunology products. For now, the strength of those franchises supports the bullish case, but sustained expansion in neuroscience, oncology, and aesthetics would prove significant if AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV) is to maintain its momentum over the longer term. title: ABBV Stock Gains On Winning FDA Approval For Rare Blood Cancer Drug - Stocktwits
content: AbbVie (ABBV) share price gained on Wednesday after U.S. Federal health regulators approved the company’s drug tailored to combat an ultra-rare, aggressive form of blood cancer. The Food and Drug Administration announced its approval of pivekimab sunirine-pvzy (sold under the brand name Decnupaz, made by AbbVie) on Wednesday. The drug is classified as an antibody-drug conjugate (a targeted therapy that pairs a cancer-seeking antibody with a potent cell-killing drug), specifically designed to bind to a protein commonly found on these cancer cells. The FDA based its decision on data from an open-label (a study where both doctors and participants know which treatment is being given), single-arm clinical trial known as CADENZA. The study tracked both newly diagnosed patients and those with recurrent cancer. Among 33 patients who were treatment-naïve (patients who have never received any previous medical treatment for their illness), the results were highly encouraging. Roughly 69.7% of these individuals achieved a complete remission or a clinical complete remission (a state where tumors shrink completely and blood counts normalize, even if minor skin lesions remain). For these patients, the response lasted an average of 9.7 months. The drug also showed measurable, though lower, activity in patients with relapsed or refractory (cancer that has returned or stopped responding to prior treatments) forms of the disease. In that group of 51 patients, 15.7% achieved a complete remission, lasting an average of 9.2 months. The FDA required the medication to feature a Boxed Warning—the agency's most prominent safety alert—warning doctors and patients about the potential for severe hepatotoxicity (liver damage). Specifically, the treatment can trigger hepatic veno-occlusive disease (a rare, life-threatening condition where the small blood vessels inside the liver become blocked and inflamed). Detroit's ‘Big Three’ automakers have reportedly received preliminary approval from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) for industrial bank charters, joining a growing list of financial technology companies, crypto firms, and household-name brands seeking to become banks under the Trump administration. Ford Motor (F), General Motors (GM), and Stellantis (STLA) — the parent company of Chrysler, Jeep, and Ram — each received preliminary deposit-insurance approval from the FDIC for industrial banks, according to a report by The New York Times. Ford’s stock rose nearly 4% in midday trade. The automakers are not alone with the list of companies now seeking or holding bank charters, according to the report. It said that PayPal (PYPL), the payments giant with over 400 million active accounts, has an application under review. So does Affirm (AFRM), the buy now, pay later pioneer that processes billions in consumer credit annually without a banking license of its own. On the crypto side, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) granted conditional national trust bank charters late last year to five crypto ventures, including Ripple Labs, and Fidelity Digital Assets. The charters allow the operators to act as custodians for customers' assets, including cryptocurrency. World Liberty Financial (WLFI), the crypto venture linked to the Trump family, is also among the applicants. Upstart Holdings (UPST), the AI-powered lending platform that underwrote $11 billion in home equity, auto, and personal loans last year, announced in March that it would seek to become a national bank holding company subject to Federal Reserve supervision. Annie Delgado, Upstart's chief risk officer, is the intended chief executive of Upstart Bank if the charter is granted, the report said. Enova (ENVA) and OppFi (OPFI), both of which specialize in short-term consumer lending, are each seeking to obtain charters by acquiring existing nationally chartered banks. For most of these firms, the appeal is straightforward. A banking charter eliminates the need for third-party partner banks to hold customer funds, extend credit, or process payments. An approval would cut costs, increases control, and in the case of a national charter, provide federal pre-emption that allows the holder to operate under a single set of rules across all 50 states rather than navigating a patchwork of state-level regulations. Automakers like Ford, GM, and Stellantis all already operate captive finance subsidiaries that provide auto loans and leases. This includes Ford Motor Credit, GM Financial, and Stellantis Financial Services. An industrial bank charter would give each company more direct control over the funding and management of those loans, potentially lowering their cost of capital and expanding the financial products they can offer customers. The Trump administration has publicly encouraged new entrants into the banking system. Shortly after President Donald Trump began his second term, FDIC leadership called for increased competition in banking. Jonathan Gould, the head of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, reinforced that position during a Blockchain Association event in December. “New charters ensure a diverse banking sector,” Gould said at the time. “Innovation, competition and fair access should always triumph over regulatory stagnation.” The surge in applications comes during the most active period for new bank charters in more than 15 years. title: AbbVie stock holds near highs as new lung cancer data and Q2 2026 growth reshape the outlook - Ad-hoc-news.de
content: AbbVie stock is trading close to its recent high as fresh Q2 2026 revenue growth, stronger Skyrizi and Rinvoq sales, raised full-year guidance, and new lung cancer data presented at WCLC 2026 support the company’s long-term story. AbbVie Inc. (US00287Y1091) stock is trading close to its recent high as investors weigh strong Q2 2026 growth, raised full-year guidance, and new lung cancer data presented at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer as of August 21, 2026. Recent market data show AbbVie shares opening at $265.62 on the latest trading session, a level that sits above a last reported close of $261.07, underscoring modest recent gains and a year-to-date advance of 14.26% as of early July 2026. Per consensus figures compiled in current coverage, the stock carries a rating of Moderate Buy and an average price target of $275.95, leaving a gap of more than $10 between the latest open and the targeted level. For investors, the combination of near-peak trading levels, double-digit revenue growth, and an expanding oncology pipeline makes the AbbVie story more about execution on new therapies than the lingering Humira patent cliff. According to a recent pharmaceutical industry overview on Q2 2026 performance, AbbVie’s net revenue for Q2 2026 rose 10.2% to $17.0 billion, reflecting broad-based growth across its immunology and oncology portfolios for the quarter ended in June 2026. This double-digit increase provides a concrete sign that the company is returning to growth even as Humira faces ongoing biosimilar competition in major markets. The same Q2 2026 review indicates that Skyrizi generated revenue of $5.5 billion in the quarter, while Rinvoq contributed $2.5 billion, with both products delivering year-over-year growth rates of 24.0% and 23.7%, respectively. Together, these two immunology drugs produced $8.03 billion in sales during Q2 2026, more than 10 times the $756 million recorded by Humira, whose revenue declined 36.1% from the prior-year period. This numerical shift illustrates how quickly AbbVie has diversified away from its legacy blockbuster. Historically, Humira dominated AbbVie’s sales mix, but in Q2 2026 Skyrizi and Rinvoq together generated over ten times Humira’s revenue, signaling a decisive transition toward newer therapies that can sustain long-term growth beyond the patent cliff era. Management used the Q2 2026 momentum to raise full-year guidance, lifting projected 2026 net revenue to $67.6 billion. The higher outlook reflects confidence that immunology demand and new indications can carry the business, even as older molecules mature and competitive pressures intensify. The updated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $67.6 billion represents a step up from prior expectations and underpins the supportive consensus view on AbbVie stock. With Q2 2026 net revenue at $17.0 billion, the implied run-rate suggests that management expects continued solid performance in the back half of the year, helped by expanding use of Skyrizi and Rinvoq and incremental contributions from newer oncology assets. Recent coverage summarizing market data shows AbbVie shares opening at $265.62 on the most recent trading day, while a market quote snapshot lists a last close at $261.07 with a 3.99% single-day gain and a year-to-date performance of 14.26% as of July 2, 2026. At these levels, AbbVie trades below the average analyst price target of $275.95, placing the stock more than 4% under the consensus fair value implied by current models. The spread between the $265.62 open and the $275.95 target highlights that analysts see room for further upside if the company can deliver on its raised guidance and pipeline milestones. In addition, various portfolio filings reported in current data show institutional investors maintaining and adjusting sizable positions in AbbVie, reinforcing the view that the stock remains a core holding for many long-horizon strategies focused on pharma and biotech income and growth. For valuation-focused investors, the key question is whether the strong immunology growth and improving oncology traction can sustain mid-single- to low-double-digit top-line expansion beyond 2026, thereby supporting current price levels and the consensus target. Beyond immunology, AbbVie has been emphasizing its oncology pipeline, and new lung cancer data presented at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC 2026) provide important context. According to a company announcement reported in current healthcare coverage, AbbVie showcased new clinical data across multiple lung cancer programs, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC). One detailed report on the WCLC 2026 presentations notes that AbbVie unveiled efficacy and safety updates for investigational therapies such as ABBV-1480, telisotuzumab adizutecan, and ABBV-706. These molecules are being evaluated across various lung cancer settings, with the clinical data focused on response rates, durability, and tolerability in both NSCLC and SCLC populations. The same WCLC 2026 overview explains that AbbVie is pursuing an expanded set of lung cancer trials, positioning these programs as a potential contributor to the company’s future oncology portfolio and longer-term growth profile. The company emphasized that telisotuzumab adizutecan and ABBV-706 remain investigational and are not approved by any health authorities worldwide, underscoring that the lung cancer work is still in the development stage rather than a current commercial driver. In the broader pipeline context, AbbVie has also announced plans for a $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics to extend its immunology portfolio into dermatology and respiratory disease. When combined with the lung cancer programs, these moves suggest a strategy focused on deepening the company’s presence in immune-mediated and oncology conditions with high unmet need. For investors tracking catalysts, the WCLC 2026 data serve as a forward-looking narrative element: while they do not immediately translate into revenue, they help frame potential future indications and market segments that could complement Skyrizi and Rinvoq as growth drivers later in the decade. Skyrizi, a monoclonal antibody targeting IL-23, and Rinvoq, a JAK inhibitor, have become the cornerstone of AbbVie’s post-Humira immunology strategy. In Q2 2026, their combined $8.03 billion in revenue and growth rates above 20% demonstrate how effectively the company has positioned these drugs across psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, and other immune-mediated conditions. The Q2 2026 figures show that Skyrizi alone generated $5.5 billion in quarterly revenue, reflecting broad adoption and increasing penetration in existing indications. Rinvoq’s $2.5 billion in revenue, paired with its 23.7% year-over-year growth, signals that AbbVie is successfully leveraging the drug’s label expansion strategy, adding new autoimmune indications over time. On the oncology side, the investigational lung cancer agents highlighted at WCLC 2026 complement AbbVie’s existing hematology and oncology portfolio. ABBV-1480, telisotuzumab adizutecan, and ABBV-706 are being studied in diverse lung cancer cohorts, and the latest data presentations underscore the company’s commitment to building a multi-asset pipeline that could one day rival its immunology franchise in scale. Historically, Humira’s $756 million in Q2 2026 revenue, down 36.1% from the prior-year quarter, reminds investors that legacy product decline remains part of the AbbVie story. Yet the magnitude of the Skyrizi and Rinvoq contribution compared with Humira illustrates that the company has already passed an important inflection point in repositioning its portfolio. Skyrizi serves as a representative product for understanding AbbVie’s current trajectory. Approved for multiple inflammatory indications, Skyrizi is administered as a subcutaneous injection and targets IL-23, a cytokine involved in autoimmune disease pathways. The drug has become widely used in plaque psoriasis, often competing with other biologics that also target IL-23 or related cytokines. In Q2 2026, Skyrizi’s $5.5 billion in revenue underscores its position as one of the largest single products in AbbVie’s lineup. The 24.0% year-over-year growth rate from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026 indicates that the company is still expanding the drug’s reach, both by gaining share in existing indications and by adding new label approvals and geographies. For patients, Skyrizi’s clinical data have highlighted durable skin clearance and symptom relief, while for AbbVie, the drug offers a long-dated patent runway that can support sustainable cash flows. As more real-world data accumulate and physicians gain experience with the therapy, AbbVie is likely to continue emphasizing Skyrizi’s role in differentiated outcomes, especially in difficult-to-treat patient subsets. A prior close of $261.07 as of July 2, 2026, was associated with a single-day gain of 3.99% and a year-to-date advance of 14.26% at that point, indicating solid performance for the stock during 2026. The gap between the $265.62 open and the average price target of $275.95 highlights that current trading levels remain below the consensus fair value derived from recent analyst models. For investors, this spread suggests that if AbbVie can continue delivering double-digit top-line growth, progress on lung cancer trials, and successful integration of planned acquisitions such as Apogee Therapeutics, the stock may have scope to trend closer to the consensus target.
